newsitem.title: USA: Landmark breast implant case goes to the jury. [CORRECTED 01:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Landmark breast implant case goes to the jury. [CORRECTED 01:00 GMT]

text.p: Dow Corning Co., in closing arguments of a landmark class-action lawsuit against the chemical giant, on Thursday denied accusations that silicone breast implants were dangerous and that it knew it.

The nearly 1,800 women who brought the suit alleged Dow Chemical was liable for their illnesses because it tested silicone compounds for Dow Corning Inc., its joint venture with Corning Inc. Dow Corning manufactured the implants.

Before a packed courtroom, plaintiffs attorney John O'Quinn told the seven-man, (correcting number of men from six to seven) six-woman jury that Dow Chemical's own research showed silicone implants could cause chronic and in some cases life-threatening illnesses.
But he charged that Dow Chemical kept silent about the danger while the safety and benefits of breast implants were trumpeted to thousands of women.
Women were told "it's all benefit, there's no risk, it can't hurt you, don't worry about it, put it in your body, forget about it," O'Quinn said.

O'Quinn said the trial, which began March 27, was a "historic case about the wrong done to these people" and urged the jurors "not to fall" for a Dow Chemical defense he said was intended to confuse them.
Dow Chemical attorney Lorna Propes categorically denied that the Midland, Mich.-based company was liable because, she said, there is no link between implants and womens' illnesses.
"We're not responsible because breast implants don't make women sick," she said. "Dow Chemical never did one thing to conceal the legitimate risks of breast implants."

Propes acknowledged that implants could lead to localized problems such as breast pain, but said they posed no more danger than any other implanted medical device such as a heart pacemaker or an articial hip joint.
She described the plaintiffs' arguments linking implants to illnesses as being "like a Texas longhorn -- a point here, a point there, lots of bull in between."

If Dow is found negligent in this first phase of the trial, a second phase will begin with the same jury considering the company's liability. The case would be dismissed if the jury decides Dow was not negligent.

Breast implant makers since 1985 have won nearly 80 percent of similar cases that have gone to trial. A Houston jury Wednesday rejected claims against Bristol-Myers Squibb Co., and a California jury last week dismissed a similar suit against a Bristol subsidiary.

In 1992, a separate Houston jury awarded $25 million to a breast implant plaintiff, but defense attorneys said the tide has turned against multi-million dollar jury awards as studies turned up no evidence linking silicone implants and illnesses.

An estimated one million women have received breast implants nationwide, about 80 percent of them for cosmetic reasons. Tens of thousands say they are suffering from serious immune system and connective tissue disorders after the implants leaked or ruptured.
